title: SQLAlchemy Deep Dive
description: Models, sessions, queries, relationships, loading strategies, migrations, transactions, raw SQL, and N+1 problems.

lessons.title: Models and Sessions
lessons.summary: Models map classes to tables; sessions track and persist unit-of-work changes.
lessons.explanation: Models map classes to tables; sessions track and persist unit-of-work changes. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: session.add(user); session.commit() persists a new row.
interview_questions: When would you apply models and sessions?
What failure mode appears when models and sessions is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Queries and Relationships
lessons.summary: ORM queries fetch mapped objects; relationships express one-to-many and many-to-many links.
lessons.explanation: ORM queries fetch mapped objects; relationships express one-to-many and many-to-many links. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: User.orders can represent a one-to-many relationship.
interview_questions: When would you apply queries and relationships?
What failure mode appears when queries and relationships is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Loading Strategies and N+1
lessons.summary: Lazy loading inside loops can trigger N+1 queries; eager loading fetches related rows earlier.
lessons.explanation: Lazy loading inside loops can trigger N+1 queries; eager loading fetches related rows earlier. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Loading 100 users then accessing orders can execute 101 queries.
interview_questions: When would you apply loading strategies and n+1?
What failure mode appears when loading strategies and n+1 is misunderstood?

lessons.title: Migrations, Transactions, and Raw SQL
lessons.summary: Migrations evolve schema; transactions protect consistency; raw SQL remains useful for complex queries.
lessons.explanation: Migrations evolve schema; transactions protect consistency; raw SQL remains useful for complex queries. In interviews, explain the concept, when it applies, and the trade-off it introduces. Use concrete examples from the provided material instead of definitions alone.
examples: Alembic records schema changes in migration files.
